texto: In the Middle Ages, a pig was put on trial. With a judge, a lawyer... and a sentence.
The year 1386. Falaise, France. A sow attacked a baby in its cradle.
But instead of just putting her down... they arrested her. And threw her in jail.
She got a real trial. The judge heard the witnesses, and found her guilty.
And for the execution, they dressed her like a person: a jacket, trousers, and gloves.
And it wasn't a one-off. In 1522, in Autun, rats were accused of devouring the crops.
Their lawyer, Bartholomew Chassenée, argued his clients couldn't come to court...
because the village cats threatened their lives on the way!
The rats never showed up. And the case, went nowhere.
Hundreds of trials like this are known across Europe. Which animal would you put on trial?
